title: Particles of the Qur'an 2: Four Words That Change a Verb
subtitle: An, lan, kay and idhan: the particles that make a verb mansoob

content.text: Particles of the Qur'an, part 2 of 5
, فِعْل مُضَارِع, "imperfect verb") normally ends in damma: يَفْعَلُ "he does". Four particles change that damma to a fatha. The verb is then in the subjunctive (
, نَصْب). If the verb ends in ن (as in تَنَالُونَ "you attain"), the ن drops instead.
The four are أَنْ "that", لَنْ "will never", كَيْ "so that" and إِذَنْ "then, in that case".
This is the particle of the verbal noun (
, حَرْف مَصْدَرِيَّة). With the verb after it, it works like a verbal noun: "that he does" is close to "his doing". So يَفْعَلُ "he does" becomes أَنْ يَفْعَلَ "that he does".

content.alt: أَمْ أَمِنتُم مَّن فِي السَّمَاءِ أَن يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكُمْ حَاصِبًا (Qur'an 67:17)

content.text: "Or do you feel safe from the One in the heaven, that He will not send against you a storm of stones?" (67:17). The verb يُرْسِلُ "he sends" has become يُرْسِلَ: it is now subjunctive (
A strong negative for the future. يَفْعَلُ "he does" becomes لَنْ يَفْعَلَ "he will never do".

content.text: "You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love" (3:92). Here تَنَالُونَ "you attain" has lost its ن: تَنَالُوا, subjunctive (

It gives the purpose of the action. In the Qur'an it usually comes with لِ: لِكَيْ "so that".

content.alt: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ لِكَيْ لَا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا (Qur'an 16:70)

content.text: "And among you is one who is brought back to the weakest age, so that he knows nothing after having known" (16:70). يَعْلَمُ "he knows" has become يَعْلَمَ, subjunctive (
It answers what was said before: "if so, then…". In the Qur'an it is written إِذًا.
